ApiKeyHelp: Routarr generates one at first start unless ROUTARR_API_KEY is set. Scripts send it as X-Api-Key. This browser sent it once to open a session, and keeps no copy.
ApiKeyHelpSession: Sign-in uses your session. This key is for clients that cannot hold one, such as scripts and monitoring, which send it as X-Api-Key.
ApiKeyKeepHint: Leave blank to keep the current key
ApiKeyMintedOnce: Copy it now. It is shown once and cannot be read again.
ApiKeyPinned: ROUTARR_API_KEY sets this key, so it cannot be changed here.
ApplicationsSubtitle: Keys for the applications that call Routarr on their own, such as a script, n8n or Home Assistant. Each key reaches only what you allow it.
ApplicationMayConfirmHelp: A question it may not answer is left to a person in Routarr. Only a key that operates is ever asked.
ApiReferenceSubtitle: The operations another application may call, with the scope each needs, as this version describes them.
ApiReferenceEnglish: The descriptions are written in English, like the API they describe.
ApiReferenceKeys: Each call sends a key made on the {screen} screen, in its X-Api-Key header.
GuardrailCapacity: Not enough room at the destination
GuardrailThreshold: More moves than the confirmation threshold
NoApplications: No application has a key yet.
ScopeOperateHelp: Sync, simulate, apply, revert, run the rule tests and take a backup.
ScopeReadHelp: Everything the screens show, except the settings, the keys and the backup archives. Every key reads.
ScopeWriteHelp: Add or remove an exception, which forces a title's category.
ScopeConfigureHelp: Create, change or remove rules, categories, folder mappings, declared destinations and rule tests: what decides where every title goes.
ApiKeyPlaintextHint: Stored in plaintext. Save the instance again to encrypt it.
ApiKeyRejected: That key was refused. Check it and try again.
ApiKeyRequired: This Routarr needs an API key
ApiKeyChooseOwn: To choose the key yourself instead, set {variable} and restart Routarr.
ProofPasswordHelp: A key outlives the session that makes it. Type the current password to go on.
ProofKeyHelp: A key outlives the session that makes it. Type the current API key to go on.
ErrorPassphraseNeeded: This archive is encrypted. Give the passphrase it was taken with.
ErrorPassphraseWrong: That passphrase does not open this archive.
ErrorPassphraseShort: A backup passphrase needs at least {min} characters.
JobDetailResealing: Converting the archives to the backup passphrase
JobDetailResealed: Archives converted: {archives}. Left as they were: {left}
BackupEncryptionHelp: Every archive carries the master key, which opens every credential Routarr stores. With a passphrase, a copy of the backups folder opens nothing without it.
BackupPassphraseKeep: Keep the passphrase somewhere else, as a password manager would: a restore on another server asks for it, and nothing opens an archive without it.
ConfirmStopEncrypting: Stop encrypting the archives? Every archive on disk is opened and kept in the clear, master key included.
PassphraseSaved: Passphrase saved. The archives on disk are being converted, see Tasks.
EncryptionStopped: Encryption stopped. The archives on disk are being opened, see Tasks.
ProofPassphraseHelp: This archive is encrypted. Type the passphrase it was taken with.
SignInAgainHelp: Sign in again at your provider first: making or removing a key needs a sign-in from the last ten minutes.
AccountHelp: The password of the account this Routarr signs in. Changing it ends every other session.
RevokeEveryKeyHelp: Every application key stops working, and the API key is replaced: the new one is shown once. For a password that leaked.
PasswordChanged: Password changed. Every other session was ended.
PasswordChangedKeysRevoked: Password changed. Every other session was ended and every key revoked.
SessionsHelp: Each browser signed in, and when. A session ends on its own after 30 days, or 24 hours through an OpenID Connect provider.
ConfirmEndSession: End this session? The browser holding it will have to sign in again.
ConfirmEndThisSession: End the session of this browser? You will have to sign in again.
ConfirmEndEverySession: End every session, this one included? Every browser will have to sign in again.
ApiKeyDockerCommand: With the Docker image, this command prints it:
ApiKeyGeneratedFile: Routarr generated it at first start and saved it as {file} next to the database. This browser sends it once to open a session, and keeps no copy.
ApplyAllHint: Applies every move this run proposed, including those beyond the displayed list, in batches.
ApplyResultWithSkipped: Decisions applied: {applied} of {requested}, no longer actionable: {skipped}.
ArrHandshakeFailed: The secure connection to {address} failed. If the port serves plain HTTP, write the address with http://. Otherwise the certificate of {service} is not one Routarr trusts.
ArrKeyRefused: {service} refused the API key. Copy it again from {service}: Settings → General → Security → API Key.
ArrMetadataAddress: A cloud host's metadata service answers at {address}, and no {service} does. Routarr does not connect there: use the address of the machine or the container running {service}.
ArrNameUnresolved: The name in {address} does not resolve. Check its spelling. In Docker, a container name resolves only when Routarr and {service} share a network.
ArrNotHttp: {address} does not answer in HTTP. If the port serves HTTPS, write the address with https://. Otherwise check the port.
ArrNotTheApi: Something answers at {address}, but not {service}'s API. Check the port, and add the URL base if {service} has one, for example {base}.
ArrProxyRefused: The request was refused before it reached {service} (HTTP 403). A proxy, a firewall rule or a sign-in policy in front of it is the likely cause.
ArrProxySignIn: Something in front of {service} asks for its own sign-in. Give Routarr an address that reaches {service} without it.
ArrProxyUnreachable: The address answers, but {service} behind it does not (HTTP {status}). Check that {service} is running, or wait until it has started.
ArrRedirectLoop: {address} redirects to itself without end. Check the URL base, and the rules of any proxy in front of {service}.
ArrRedirected: {address} redirects to another address, where Routarr does not send the API key. Enter the address it redirects to, often with https:// or a URL base.
ArrRedirectedElsewhere: {address} redirects to {host}. If {service} answers there, enter that address. If it is a sign-in page, give Routarr an address that reaches {service} without it.
ArrServerError: {service} failed on its own side (HTTP {status}). Its log says why, under System → Logs in {service}.
ArrTimedOut: {service} did not answer in time at {address}. Check the address, and that no firewall drops the connection.
ArrUnreachable: Nothing answers at {address}. Check that {service} is running, and the address and the port.
ArrUnreachableLoopback: Nothing answers at {address}. If Routarr runs in Docker, localhost is Routarr's own container: use {service}'s container name or the host's IP address instead.
ArrWrongApp: {address} answers as {found}, not {service}. Change the type, or the port: Radarr usually listens on 7878 and Sonarr on 8989.
AuditSignInHeldBack: A sign-in was held back: this address failed too often.
AuditSignInRefused: A sign-in was refused: wrong name or password.
AuditKeySessionRefused: A key that opens nothing was sent to sign in.
AuditKeySessionOpened: Signed in with the API key.
AuditOidcRefused: A sign-in through the OpenID Connect provider failed: {reason}
AuditOidcSignedIn: Signed in through the OpenID Connect provider.
AuditEverySessionEnded: Every session was ended. Sessions ended: {count}
AuditApiKeyRefused: A request was sent with a key that opens nothing.
AuditEveryKeyRevoked: Every application key was revoked and the API key replaced.
AuditApplicationKeyUnknown: An application key that does not exist or was revoked was sent: {id}
AuditApplicationKeyMade: The application key {name} ({id}) was made, with the scopes: {scopes}.
AuditApplicationKeyMadeMovingFiles: The application key {name} ({id}) was made, with the scopes: {scopes}. It may move files.
AuditScopeMissing: The application key {name} ({id}) was refused {route}, which needs the {scope} scope.
AuditOwnerRoute: The application key {name} ({id}) was refused {route}, which only the owner may call.
AuditForeignOrigin: A write from another site was refused: {origin}
AuditUnknownHost: A request was sent to {host}, a name this Routarr does not answer to.
AuditPasswordRefused: A password change was refused: the current password was wrong.
AuditProofRefused: A session asked to make or remove a key without its proof.
AuditBackupDownloaded: The archive {name} was downloaded. It carries the master key.
AuditBackupPassphraseRemoved: The backup passphrase was removed: new archives are no longer encrypted.
AuditRestoreStaged: The archive {name} was staged, to be restored at the next start.
AuditConfigurationImported: A configuration bundle was imported. Settings: {settings}, instances: {instances}, rules: {rules}
AuditSigningSecretMade: A new notification signing secret was made.
AuditSigningSecretsRemoved: The notification signing secrets were removed.
AuditEventsLost: Events lost while the security log was full: {count}

BackupCopyHint: A configuration export never contains your Arr API keys: they are sealed with a key held by this installation only. For a copy off this machine, download an archive under Backups, or copy the backups folder beside the database. A copy of routarr.db taken while Routarr runs can miss every recent change.
BackupsHelp: Taken on a schedule and kept beside the database. Each archive holds the database, the master key and the API key, everything a restore needs, which makes the file as sensitive as the key itself.
BatchApplyStopped: Stopped after a failure. Applied: {applied} of {candidates}. Batches run: {run} of {planned}. The rest is still pending.
CapacityShortWarning: {path} would receive {needed} but reports only {free} free.
CategoryNameHint: Lower-cased automatically. Letters, digits, '-' and '_' only.
CategoryNameRefused: A category name holds letters, digits, '-' and '_' only.
CategoryNameTooLong: A category name holds {max} characters at most.
ConditionCurrentRootFolderStartsWith: Current root folder is or is under '{value}'
ConditionLabelAddedWithinDays: Added within the last N days
ConditionLabelCurrentRootFolderStartsWit: Current root folder is or is under
ConditionValuesHelp: Each condition is a requirement. The values inside it combine as the selector says: any of them, or all of them.
ConditionPhraseCurrentRootFolderStartsWi: Current root folder: {value} or a folder inside it
ConditionPhraseSeriesTypeIs: Sonarr series type is one of {values}
ConditionPhraseSizeOnDiskOverGb: Size on disk: more than {value} GB
ConfigImportResult: Restored. Settings: {settings}, categories: {categories}, instances: {instances}, mappings: {folders}, rules: {rules}, exceptions: {overrides}.
ConfigImportNeedsKey: Instances waiting for their API key: {names}
ConfirmApplyItems: Items to be re-pointed in Radarr/Sonarr: {count}.
ConfirmApplyItemsWithFiles: Items to be re-pointed in Radarr/Sonarr, their files moved on disk too: {count}.
ConfirmApplyAllItems: Items to be reassigned in Radarr/Sonarr, in batches: {count}.
ConfirmApplyAllItemsWithFiles: Items to be reassigned in Radarr/Sonarr, in batches, their files moved on disk too: {count}.
ConfirmDeleteBackup: Delete the backup {name}? It is the only copy. Nothing else holds this snapshot.
ConfirmDeleteInstance: Delete "{name}"? Its media, mappings and exceptions are removed from Routarr (nothing is deleted in the Arr).
ConfirmDeleteOverride: Remove the exception on "{title}"? The rules take over again.
ConfirmRevokeApplication: Revoke the key of {name}? It stops working at once, and cannot be restored.
ConfirmPurge: Purge decisions, move log entries and task history beyond the retention window?
ConfirmRemoveKey: Remove the API key? Clients using it stop working immediately.
ConfirmRemoveDestination: Remove the destination {path}? A category mapped to it no longer routes there. Nothing is deleted on disk.
ConfirmRestore: Restore {name}? It replaces the current database and the master key. The API key, the password and every key revoked since stay as they are today, and everyone signs in again. Nothing changes until Routarr is restarted.
ConfirmRevertFiles: Move the files on disk back as well?
ConfirmRotateKey: Regenerate the API key? Every client still using the current one stops working until it is updated.
ConfirmRotateWebhookToken: Rotate the webhook token of "{name}"? The Arr's webhook stops working until the new URL is pasted into it.
ConflictDuplicateMapping: Root folders on '{instance}' mapped to '{category}': {count}, so routing would pick one arbitrarily
ConflictOrphaned: Root folder mapped to '{category}', which is no longer a known category
ConflictUnmapped: No root folder on '{instance}' is mapped to '{category}', so matching media will be skipped
DashboardSubtitle: What Routarr knows about your library and what it is waiting to do about it.
DiagnosticsSubtitle: Connectivity, metadata coverage and anything that would silently stop routing from working.
ConfirmDiscardRule: Close the rule without saving your changes?
ConfirmDiscardInstance: Close the instance without saving your changes?
ConfirmLeaveUnsaved: Leave the settings without saving? Unsaved changes: {count}
ConfirmLeaveUnsavedMappings: Leave without saving the categories picked for the folders? Unsaved changes: {count}
GuideCategoriesText: A category names where a kind of title belongs, such as anime or kids. Give each root folder the Arr reports a category, starting with the default one.
GuideComplete: Routarr is set up. Apply the moves you agree with from the simulation, whenever you are ready.
GuideInstanceText: Routarr reads your library through the Arr's own API. Add an instance with its address and API key, and Routarr syncs it at once.
GuideIntro: A few steps take Routarr from a fresh install to its first proposed moves. Each one ticks itself once it is done, so you can leave and come back at any time.
GuideLiveText: While the global dry-run is on, no move reaches Radarr or Sonarr. Turn it off once the decisions look right.
GuideMetadataText: Radarr and Sonarr already supply genres, language and certification. TMDB, AniList and the other sources add keywords and countries.
GuidePaused: The setup is not finished. Required steps done: {done} of {total}
GuidePillLabel: Getting started, required steps done: {done} of {total}
GuideRestartText: Show the getting-started steps on the dashboard again.
GuideRuleText: A rule sends the titles matching its conditions to a category. Rules run by priority, and the first that matches wins.
GuideSimulationText: A simulation proposes where each title belongs and says why. Nothing is written to Radarr or Sonarr.
GuideOptionalNext: Step {number} of {total} is done. Next, optional: {next}
GuideUnavailable: The getting-started guide could not be read: {error}
HelpCardAccount: On the Security tab when Routarr signs in with a password. Change the password, at least 12 characters, and every other session ends. Tick Also revoke every key when the password leaked: every application key stops and the API key is replaced.
HelpCardApiSchemas: Every type the operations take or return, by name. Open one to read its fields, their types, whether each is required and what it holds, when a request body or a response names it.
HelpCardApiTagBackups: The backups kept, and taking one on request. Taking one needs Operate, and an application key may take one at most every ten minutes.
HelpCardApiTagCategories: The categories, the root folders of each Arr and the category each folder leads to, with what the mappings leave unsaid. Creating, renaming or removing a category, declaring a destination the Arr does not list and mapping a folder all need Configure.
HelpCardApiTagDecisions: Running a simulation, listing the decisions it stored, and applying or reverting their moves behind the same guardrails as the interface. Every operation but the list needs Operate, and moving files needs a key allowed to. A 409 answer names the guardrail that asks in its confirm field.
HelpCardApiTagExceptions: Exceptions force a title's category and outrank every rule. Listing them only reads, and adding or removing one needs Write. The external operations name the title by its TMDB, TheTVDB or IMDb id, for an application that does not know Routarr's own ids.
HelpCardApiTagInstances: The Radarr and Sonarr instances Routarr reads, one or all, and reading them again. A sync needs Operate and answers one report per instance, and an instance that fails stops none of the others. Adding or editing an instance stays on the Instances screen.
HelpCardApiTagLibrary: The titles Routarr read from the Arrs, a page at a time or one by one, and where each one goes and why. /route answers where a title another service names would go, even one the library does not hold, and stores nothing. Every operation here only reads.
HelpCardApiTagRules: The rules in priority order, the conditions they may use, what each rule decides, and the rule tests. Changing a rule or a rule test, and judging a draft rule with validate or preview, needs Configure. Running the rule tests needs Operate, and the rest only reads.
HelpCardApiTagStatus: Whether Routarr is up and what needs attention. /ping needs no key and suits an uptime monitor, /status answers the counts and warnings without reaching anything, and /health checks every Arr and source, which needs Operate. It also holds the Prometheus metrics, the metadata sources and who a key belongs to.
HelpCardApiTagTasks: The tasks that ran in the background, how each ended and what it reported, and the move log with its CSV export. A long call sent with Prefer: respond-async answers with a task id, and that task's result holds the report once it has finished. Everything here only reads.
HelpCardArrInstances: Each Radarr and Sonarr instance as the check found it: whether it answers, the version it runs, how many titles Routarr holds from it, how many of its root folders are mapped and when it was last synced. An Error status carries its reason beside it, and zero mapped folders means its titles go nowhere.
HelpCardBackupEncryption: On the Maintenance tab, the passphrase every backup archive is sealed with, typed twice. The badge says whether archives are encrypted. Keep the passphrase elsewhere: a restore on another server asks for it.
HelpCardBackups: On the Maintenance tab, the archives kept beside the database, with their date and size. Back up now takes one, and each can be downloaded, restored or deleted. A restore replaces the database and the master key at the next restart.
HelpCardCapacityTitle: Each root folder this run would move titles into, with the number of titles, the data arriving and the free space its Arr reports. A free figure too small for what is arriving is flagged, and a warning above names that folder. Data moving within the same volume is shown apart, since it takes no extra room.
HelpCardCategories: Every category with its description, the rules using it and the folders mapped to it. Rename one with the pencil, and rules, folder mappings, exceptions and the decision history follow the new name. A category still in use cannot be deleted, and the default one has no delete button.
HelpCardDashboardInstances: Each Radarr and Sonarr instance, with whether it answers, how many titles it holds, how many of its root folders are mapped to a category and when it was last synced. Error comes with the reason the instance does not answer, and an instance with no mapped folder routes nothing. Manage opens Instances to change them.
HelpCardFolderMappings: Every root folder the instances report and every destination you declared, with its free space and its state. Pick a category in the Category column and press Save on that row to map it. The form under the table adds a destination folder for an instance, checked against that instance.
HelpCardGuideRestart: On the General tab. Show the guide brings the Getting started steps back on the dashboard and takes you there.
HelpCardGuideTitle: The setup steps from a fresh install to the first moves: connect an instance, map root folders to categories, choose metadata sources, write a rule, run a simulation and turn off the global dry-run. Each step ticks itself once done and its button opens the screen that does it, while steps marked Optional do not count in the progress. Skip the guide folds it to one line, and Show the guide on the General tab of Settings brings it back.
HelpCardHealthMetadataSources: Every metadata source in the order the rules read them, with its state as the check found it: Connected, active, needs an API key, or Error. Radarr / Sonarr reads active, since the instances above are checked on their own. The line below counts the cached entries and the titles with missing metadata, and says whether the database answers.
HelpCardLibraryFacets: What the library holds for each question a rule can ask: genres, original languages, origin countries, certifications, Arr tags, series types and root folders, each value with how many titles carry it. Check it before writing a condition, since a value the library does not carry matches nothing. A warning above the values counts titles with neither a genre nor an original language, which no metadata condition can see.
HelpCardMetadataTitle: What the metadata sources say about this title: genres, original language, origin countries, certification, keywords, status and synopsis. The sources line names every source that contributed, in priority order, and the status and the synopsis each name their source. When no source has answered, a warning stands in its place.
HelpCardNotificationTest: On the Notifications tab. Sends a message to the saved address in the saved format, signed like the others, so save a change before testing it. The result says whether the receiver accepted it.
HelpCardPreviewTitle: What the rule being edited would change in the library, with nothing saved yet. It counts the titles changing category and how the moves required and the unclassified titles would change, then lists titles that change with their category before and after. Issues with the rule are shown above the figures.
HelpCardRoutarrApiKey: On the Security tab, the key scripts and monitoring send as X-Api-Key. Create or Regenerate it, confirm it is you when asked, and copy it at once: it is shown once. When ROUTARR_API_KEY sets the key, it cannot be changed here.
HelpCardRuleEvaluation: Every enabled rule that applies to this title's media type and instance, in the order the engine reads them, with its priority, its category and its outcome: winner, excluded, matched with lower priority, or did not match. Under each rule, every condition shows whether it held, what it expected and what the title carries. An exclusion that vetoed a rule is named under it.
HelpCardSessions: Each browser signed in, with when its session opened, was last used and ends. End one left open on a shared machine, or Sign out everywhere. Ending the one marked This browser signs you out.
HelpCardSettingsMetadataCoverage: What the sources are asked and how long their answers stay: the titles AniList and MyAnimeList are searched for, the OMDb requests a day, the cache lifetime and the certification regions. A change waits in the save bar until you press Save.
HelpCardSettingsMetadataSources: The sources Routarr asks, split into Active, in priority order and Inactive. Move a source up or down, enable or disable it, and paste the API key of TMDB, OMDb or TheTVDB in its row. Radarr / Sonarr cannot be disabled, only moved, and Save writes the order and the keys together.
HelpCardSettingsTabAutomation: Background sync, Simulate after each sync, Automatic application and the Scheduler tick. With global dry-run off and automatic application on, a warning says that decisions for titles with no files are written without confirmation.
HelpCardSettingsTabGeneral: The Language of the interface and of the messages Routarr writes, and the Theme. A language not fully translated shows its percentage, and Automatic follows the operating system.
HelpCardSettingsTabGuardrails: Global dry-run, Default category, Batch limit and Confirmation threshold. While global dry-run is on, nothing is written to Radarr or Sonarr. Turning it off shows a warning above the tabs.
HelpCardSettingsTabMaintenance: Scheduled backups, their interval and how many are kept, and how long decisions and the move log are retained. Export configuration and Import configuration copy the setup without the Arr API keys, and Purge now removes what is past retention.
HelpCardSettingsTabNotifications: The Notification webhook address, its format and the extra events to send: Failed syncs, Finished simulations and Finished moves. The address is stored encrypted and never exported, and removing it turns notifications off.
HelpCardSettingsTabSecurity: How many days the security log keeps its events, 0 keeping them all. The link under it opens the security log, which lists sign-ins, key changes and refusals.
HelpCardSourceCreditsTitle: The credit each source's terms ask for, with a link to its site. Every source Routarr can ask over the network is credited, enabled or not.
HelpCardSourceRefreshTitle: A Read again button for each saved source Routarr asks over the network. Use it after a source has corrected its data, instead of waiting for the cache lifetime to pass. The result counts the answers read again and those that failed.
HelpCardWebhookSigning: On the Notifications tab. Generate a signing secret so the receiver can check each notification came from Routarr, and copy it at once: it is shown once. Replacing it keeps the old secret signing beside the new one for a day.
HelpFixApiReference1: Make a key on the Applications screen and send it in the X-Api-Key header. It is shown once, so a lost key is replaced by a new one.
HelpFixApiReference2: The badge on the operation names the scope. Scopes are set when a key is made, so create a key that allows it on Applications and revoke the old one.
HelpFixApiReference3: Send the name it gives in confirm back in your request's confirm list. When answerable is false the key may not answer it: make a key that may on Applications, or apply from Routarr's Simulation screen.
HelpFixApiReference4: The search reads the path, the method and the one-line summary, not the descriptions. Try a word of the path, such as decisions or rules.
HelpFixApplications1: A key is shown once and cannot be read again. Create a new key with the same rights, then revoke the old one.
HelpFixApplications2: A key outlives the session that makes it. Type the current password or API key, or sign in again at your provider when your sign-in is older than ten minutes.
HelpFixApplications3: A key's scopes cannot be changed: create a key that allows the scope named in the refusal, which the security log also records, then revoke the old one.
HelpFixApplications4: The question is left to a person: apply those decisions from the Simulation screen, or create a key allowed to answer that guardrail.
HelpFixAuditHistory1: A run records no decision for a title already in its right folder, and the list hides decisions a newer run replaced unless you check "Include decisions replaced by a newer run". To see where any title goes and why, find it on Library and press "Why?".
HelpFixAuditHistory2: The message is the reason Radarr, Sonarr or Routarr gave. Fix what it names, then run a simulation and apply the move again on the Simulation screen.
HelpFixAuditHistory3: Only the latest applied move of a title can be reverted, and only while the title is still in the folder that move put it in and the folder it came from is still a root folder of its instance. Look for the newest Applied row of the same title.
HelpFixAuditHistory4: Nothing is written to Radarr or Sonarr while dry-run is on. Turn off Global dry-run in Settings, on the Guardrails tab, then revert again.
HelpFixDashboard1: The reason is written beside it. On Instances, check its Base URL and API key with Test connectivity, then press Refresh here.
HelpFixDashboard2: Press Diagnostics to see every warning. Most of them name the screen or the setting that clears them.
HelpFixDashboard3: Open the move log and filter by Failure to read what the Arr answered. Fix the cause, then run a simulation again so the title gets a new decision.
HelpFixDashboard4: Rules on genre, keyword or certification cannot classify those titles yet. Check on Metadata sources that the sources you rely on are listed with their keys, and the titles are asked again at the next pass.
HelpFixDiagnostics1: Edit the instance on the Instances screen and check its Base URL and API key with Test connectivity. Then press Re-check here.
HelpFixDiagnostics2: Titles of an unmapped category are skipped until it leads somewhere. On Categories and folders, choose a category for a root folder of each instance and save.
HelpFixDiagnostics3: Enter or correct its key on the Metadata sources screen, or take the source out of the list. What only that source provides cannot match until then.
HelpFixDiagnostics4: The Enrich task after each sync fills them in at each source's pace, which you can follow on Tasks. If the count stays, check on Metadata sources that a source able to describe these titles is listed with its key.
HelpFixInstances1: Press Add instance, choose Radarr or Sonarr, fill in the base URL and the API key, and press Test connectivity before saving.
HelpFixInstances2: With Routarr in Docker, localhost is Routarr's own container: use the Arr's container name or the host's IP address, with the port and the URL base if it has one. A container name resolves only when both containers share a network.
HelpFixInstances3: Copy the key again in the Arr under Settings, General, Security, paste it in the API key field and save. After a change of address, the stored key has to be typed again.
HelpFixInstances4: The date is the last sync that worked, and the reason shows under Failed. Correct the address or the key with Edit, or raise the variable the message names, then press Sync now on that row.
HelpFixLogs1: Only an apply or a revert writes here, and Global dry-run stays on until you turn it off in Settings, on the Guardrails tab. Then apply moves from the Simulation screen.
HelpFixLogs2: The message is the reason the Arr or Routarr gave, such as an instance that does not answer or is disabled. Fix it on the Instances screen, then run a simulation and apply the move again.
HelpFixLogs3: The apply ran with "Move the files on disk too" left off, so only the library entry was re-pointed. Revert it on History without moving files, then run a simulation and apply it again with that box checked.
HelpFixLogs4: Entries older than Log retention (days), in Settings on the Maintenance tab, are removed. Raise it to keep more, or set it to 0 to keep every entry.
HelpFixMediaExplorer1: If a search or a filter is set, press Clear filters. Otherwise nothing is synced yet: sync an instance on Instances.
HelpFixMediaExplorer2: No simulation has read this title yet, as happens to a title synced after the last run. Run a simulation.
HelpFixMediaExplorer3: No enabled metadata source has answered for it, so genre, keyword and certification conditions cannot match it. Press Why?, then Ask the sources again, and if none answers, check the source list on Metadata sources.
HelpFixMediaExplorer4: Why? evaluates the rules as they stand, while the column shows the last simulation. Run a simulation to bring the column up to date.
HelpFixMetadataSources1: These sources need an API key of your own. Paste it in the field of that source's row, press Enable, then Save.
HelpFixMetadataSources2: Radarr and Sonarr report neither. Enable a source that does, such as TMDB with its key, and Save: titles are asked after the next sync.
HelpFixMetadataSources3: Paste a valid key in that source's row, which replaces the stored one, and Save.
HelpFixMetadataSources4: The titles still to enrich are asked after midnight UTC. If your OMDb key allows more, raise OMDb requests a day under Cache and coverage and Save.
HelpFixOverrides1: An exception only sets the category. Run a simulation to get the move, then apply it there.
HelpFixOverrides2: It searches the titles synced from your instances by part of their title. If the library is empty, sync an instance on Instances first.
HelpFixOverrides3: Its forced category has no root folder on the title's instance. Map the category on Categories and folders, then run the simulation again.
HelpFixOverrides4: Pick a title in the search results first. The button waits for a selected title.
HelpFixRootFolders1: Add an instance and sync it. Its root folders appear here once the sync is done.
HelpFixRootFolders2: Pick that category in the Category column of a folder on that instance and press Save on the row. If no folder fits, add a destination folder under the table first.
HelpFixRootFolders3: The Arr could not reach it, often a NAS asleep or a share not mounted. Make the disk reachable from the Arr, then sync the instance so its state is read again.

HelpPurposeApiReference: The API reference lists every operation another application may call, such as a script, n8n, Home Assistant or a dashboard, grouped by area, with the scope each needs, its parameters, its responses and a curl example. It is read from the running version, so it matches what this Routarr answers. Make the key on the Applications screen, and download openapi.json for tools that read OpenAPI.
HelpPurposeApplications: Applications gives keys to programs that call Routarr on their own, such as a script, n8n or Home Assistant. Every key can read, and reaches only the scopes, the guardrail answers and the file moves you allow it. Come here to create a key for a new integration, and to revoke one that is unused or has leaked.
HelpPurposeAuditHistory: History lists every decision Routarr recorded: the category and target root folder a run chose for each title, the rule behind it, its confidence and what became of it. Come here to see why a title went where it did, to find a move that failed, or to put an applied move back with Revert. Search a title, filter by status, and include the decisions a newer run replaced when you need them.
HelpPurposeDashboard: The Dashboard sums up what Routarr knows about your library and what it is waiting to do. On a fresh install it holds the Getting started guide, which leads you through setup one step at a time. Later, come here to see how many decisions are pending, whether each instance answers and whether any move failed. Simulation opens the screen where pending decisions are reviewed and applied.
HelpPurposeDiagnostics: Diagnostics checks every Arr instance and metadata source live, and lists every warning that would quietly stop routing: an instance that does not answer, a category with no folder, a missing key, a failed backup. Come here when the navigation shows a warning count or when titles stop moving. Re-check runs every check again.
HelpPurposeInstances: Instances lists the Radarr and Sonarr servers Routarr reads from and writes to. Add one with its address and API key, test the connection, and sync it to read its library and root folders. Come back here to fix an address or a key, to sync on demand, or to copy the webhook address that tells Routarr about a new title right away.
HelpPurposeLogs: The move log records every write Routarr made to Radarr and Sonarr: each move an apply sent and each revert, with when it happened, what set it off, the title, the root folders involved and whether it worked. Come here to check what changed in your Arrs, or to read why a move failed. Search by title or details, filter by outcome, and export the matching entries as CSV.
HelpPurposeMediaExplorer: The Library lists every title synced from Radarr and Sonarr, with its instance, its current root folder, the category the last simulation decided and whether metadata is known. Search, filter by type, or tick Unclassified only to find the titles no rule matched. Why? opens the full explanation of where a title goes, where you can ask the sources again or pin the decision as a test.
HelpPurposeMetadataSources: Metadata sources chooses where Routarr reads genres, keywords, countries and ratings for each title, beyond what Radarr and Sonarr report. You order the sources, enable or disable them, give the API keys some of them need, and set how long their answers are kept. Come here when a rule needs data the Arr does not give, such as keywords or origin countries, or when a warning names this screen.
HelpPurposeOverrides: Exceptions force the category of single titles by hand, for the few the rules get wrong. An exception outranks every rule, whatever its priority. Create one with New exception by searching the library and choosing a category, and delete it to hand the title back to the rules. The move itself comes from the next simulation.
HelpPurposeRootFolders: Categories and folders is where you create the categories your rules route to and map the folders of each instance to them. A title goes to the folder mapped to its category on its own instance, so a category with no folder there routes nothing. Come here after the first sync of an instance, and whenever you add a category or a folder.
HelpPurposeRulesEngine: Rules decide which category each title belongs to. Each rule holds conditions, optional exclusions and a target category, and rules are read by priority: the first that matches wins. Come here to write, reorder, import or export rules, and to spot rules that decide nothing. In the editor, Preview impact shows what a rule would change before you save it.
HelpPurposeRuleTests: Rule tests keep the decisions you rely on from changing unnoticed when rules change. Each test is a title pinned with its metadata to the category it must keep landing in. Run tests after editing rules: a failing test says where the title goes now. Pin a test from a title's explanation, opened with Why? in the Library.
HelpPurposeSecurityLog: The security log records every sign-in, every refusal and every change to a key, the password, a backup or the settings, with who asked and from which address. Come here to check who signed in, to spot an address that keeps being refused, or to confirm that a key was made or revoked. Only the owner reads it: no application key can, whatever its scopes.
HelpPurposeSettings: Settings holds how Routarr behaves as a whole, in six tabs: General, Security, Guardrails, Automation, Notifications and Maintenance. Here you set the language, the API key and sessions, the guardrails every apply passes, what runs unattended, where notifications go, and backups and retention. A changed field waits in the save bar, and Save writes every tab together.
HelpPurposeSimulation: The Simulation evaluates every rule against the whole library and lists the resulting decisions, each with the rule that chose it and why, before anything is written. Come here after changing rules or exceptions, or when decisions are waiting for review. Select the moves you agree with and apply them, or apply every move of the run at once with Apply all.
HelpPurposeTasks: Tasks lists every background run with what set it off, its status, its progress and how it ended: syncs, enrichment, simulations, applies, reverts, backups and maintenance. Come here when something seems not to happen, to follow a long apply, or to read why a run failed. A running apply or revert can be stopped with Stop on its row.

WarnApiUnauthenticated: The API is unauthenticated. Set ROUTARR_AUTH to apikey, forms or oidc to require a sign-in.

WarnDataDiskLow: The disk holding Routarr's data has {free} left, less than a backup needs. Free some space before the database or a backup fails.

WarnNoEnabledInstance: No enabled Arr instance, so there is nothing to route.
WarnProviderNeedsKey: {provider} is in the source list but has no API key: what only it provides cannot match.

WarnProviderUnreachable: {provider} is configured but does not answer.
WarnProviderRateLimited: {provider} asked for fewer requests. Routarr keeps to its pace and asks again later.
WarnProviderKeyRefused: {provider} refused its key. Check it on the Metadata sources screen.
WarnProviderQuota: {provider} has used the requests it may send today. The titles still to enrich are asked after midnight (UTC).
WarnSchedulerPanicked: Unattended background passes that failed in the last 24 hours: {count}. Syncing continued, but check the server log.
WarnSettingAboveMaximum: Setting '{key}' is {value}, above the maximum of {max}. It stays as it is until it is saved lower.
WarnBackupPassphraseUnreadable: The backup passphrase cannot be opened with the master key in place, so no backup is taken. Set the passphrase again in Settings.
WarnUnmappedCategories: Categories not mapped to any root folder: {count}. Matching media will be skipped.

WebhookUrlCopied: Webhook URL copied to the clipboard
WebhookUrlCopyFailed: The browser blocked the clipboard. Webhook URL: {url}

HintLogs: Every write to Radarr and Sonarr

HintApplications: Keys for scripts and other applications

ErrorTargetNeverReached: '{path}' has never answered. Applying now may fail.
ConflictUnreachableFor: Root folder '{path}' has not answered for {age}
DeclareDestinationHelp: A folder the instance can reach, even one it does not list as a root folder. Declare one root folder in Radarr or Sonarr and name the targets beneath it here. The path is checked against that instance, not against this machine.
ApplyReplaced: Replaced since by other moves, not applied: {count}.
ApplyStillMoving: Still moving in the Arr: {count}. The next sync confirms each move.
ApplyStoppedByDryRun: Stopped when the dry-run was turned on: the rest was not attempted.
ApplyStoppedForShutdown: Stopped as Routarr shut down: the rest was not attempted.
ApplyStoppedOnRequest: Stopped on request: the rest was not attempted.
ErrorCapacityUnknown: '{path}' does not report free space, and it sits under no known root folder. {needed} would be moved without anything checking the room.
ErrorDestinationAbsolute: A destination is an absolute path: /data/movies on Linux, D:\Movies or \\server\share on Windows.
ErrorDestinationAlreadyListed: '{path}' is already listed for this instance
ErrorDestinationTwoSlashes: A path opening with two slashes is a share on Windows and a plain folder on Linux. Write a Windows share with backslashes, as \\server\share, and a Linux path with one slash.
ErrorDestinationUnseen: The instance cannot see '{path}'. Check the path as that container sees it.
ErrorDestinationNotOurs: That folder comes from the instance. Remove it there instead
ErrorCategoryAlreadyMapped: Category '{category}' is already mapped to '{path}' on this instance
ConfirmStopTask: Stop this task before its next move? What already reached Radarr or Sonarr stays done, and the rest is left as it was.
ErrorDestinationNotPlain: Write the folder without "..", "." or an empty segment: {path}
ErrorInstanceNameTaken: An instance is already named {name}. Give this one another name.
ErrorMoveNotMade: {arr} holds the title in {path}: the move was not made, or was undone.
ErrorMoveUndone: {arr} put the title back in {path}: its files could not be moved.
ErrorNotEnoughSpaceShared: {paths} sit on one volume: together they would receive {needed}, and it reports {free} free.
SigningSecretUnreadable: The signing secret cannot be opened with this installation's key, so no notification is sent. Replace the secret.
SigningSecretMintedOnce: Copy it now. It is shown once and cannot be read again.
ErrorPreviewsWaiting: Previews are already waiting for the library. Try again once one has finished.
ErrorProposalsReplaced: A newer simulation replaced these decisions with other moves. Review the latest simulation and apply again.
ErrorPurgeRunning: A purge is already running. Try again once it has finished.
ErrorTaskNotCancellable: This task can no longer be stopped: it has ended, or it is not an apply or a revert.
JobDetailAppliedBatchesMoving: Applied: {applied}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}, batches run: {run} of {planned}
JobDetailCancelled: Stopped on request. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
JobDetailStoppedByDryRun: Stopped when the dry-run was turned on. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
JobDetailStoppedForShutdown: Stopped as Routarr shut down. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
SettingNotificationFormatHelp: How each notification is written. Automatic recognises a Discord webhook and a topic on ntfy.sh, and sends Routarr's JSON to any other address. Choose ntfy for a topic on your own server, Gotify for its message address with an application token, and Apprise for an Apprise API address. Routarr's JSON carries the event, its severity and its ids for another application.
NotificationTestHelp: Sends a message to the saved address, in the saved format and signed like the others. Save a change before testing it.
NotificationTestSent: The receiver accepted the test notification.
NotificationTestNoAddress: No notification webhook address is saved. Save one, then send the test again.
NotificationTestRefused: The receiver refused the test notification with HTTP {status}. Check the address and the format.
NotificationTestUnreachable: The test notification did not reach the address. Check that it is right and that Routarr can reach it.
RadarrBelowVersion: Radarr {version} is older than {minimum}, the oldest release Routarr supports in full: a film it adds is routed at the next sync, not before it downloads.
RequestedHint: The Arr is moving the files. The next sync confirms the move.
SonarrBelowVersion: Sonarr {version} is older than {minimum}, the oldest release Routarr supports in full: a series it adds is routed at the next sync, not before it downloads, and its original language is unknown.
TaskStopRequested: Stop requested: the task ends before its next move.
TermTextApplicationKey: A key made on the Applications screen for one program, such as a script or Home Assistant, sent as X-Api-Key. It reaches only what its scopes allow, is shown once when created, cannot be edited, and stops working at once when revoked.
TermTextApply: Carrying out decisions: Routarr asks Radarr or Sonarr to change each title's root folder, one title at a time, and to move its files on disk too if you tick that box. Every apply passes the guardrails first, and each write is recorded in the move log.
TermTextArrApiKey: The key Radarr or Sonarr shows under Settings, General, Security. Routarr stores it encrypted and sends it only to the address it was saved with.
TermTextAutoApply: Applies a decision as soon as it is made, without a click, but only for titles with no files yet, so nothing moves on disk. Global dry-run still blocks it.
TermTextBackup: An archive of the database, the master key and the API key, kept beside the database. Without a passphrase it is as sensitive as the key itself.
TermTextBaseUrl: The address Routarr reaches the instance at, with the port and the URL base if the Arr has one. In Docker, localhost is Routarr's own container, so use the Arr's container name or the host's IP address.
TermTextBatchLimit: The most items a single apply may touch. A whole simulation is applied in slices of this size, after a confirmation.
TermTextCachedEntries: Answers from the metadata sources that Routarr keeps, so the sources are not asked the same question again and again.
TermTextCategory: A named destination that rules and exceptions send titles to, such as anime or kids. Names are lower-cased, and a category leads to a folder only through a folder mapping on each instance.
TermTextCertificationRegions: Country codes, most preferred first, such as FR, US. When several sources rate a title, the rating of the first region wins whatever the order of the sources.
TermTextCondition: One test a rule makes on a title, such as its genre, original language or current root folder. The rule's logic says whether ALL conditions must hold or ANY one is enough.
TermTextConfidence: How strongly the winning rule's conditions agree, as a percentage: more conditions that hold raise it, and a rule needing ALL conditions starts higher than one needing ANY. An exception scores in full, a title no rule matched scores zero, and no setting acts on it.
TermTextConfirmationThreshold: Above this many items, an apply asks for a second, explicit confirmation.
TermTextDecision: What one run of the rules chose for one title: its category, the root folder that category leads to on its instance, the rule behind it and why. A decision that moves a title stays Pending until you apply it, which makes it Applied or Failed.
TermTextDefaultCategory: The category a title gets when no rule matches it, shown as default category in the Rule column. It is chosen on the Guardrails tab of Settings, and cannot be deleted while it is the default.
TermTextDestination: A folder you declare for an instance although the Arr does not list it as a root folder, usually one beneath a root folder. Only a declared destination can be removed, on Categories and folders.
TermTextDryRun: While it is on, Routarr refuses every write to Radarr and Sonarr, whatever you click, and simulations still run so you can review their decisions. A new install starts with it on, and it is turned off on the Guardrails tab of Settings.
TermTextEnrichment: Asks the metadata sources about the titles a sync brought in, at the pace each source allows. It runs after every sync, and the rules read what it found.
TermTextException: A category you force on one title by hand. It outranks every rule whatever their priority, and holds until you delete it.
TermTextExclusion: A condition that vetoes its rule: when it holds, the rule does not decide for that title and the next rule is read. The rule list shows exclusions after the word except.
TermTextFailedDecisions: Titles whose latest move failed and that no run has looked at since. The next simulation settles each one, with a new decision or by finding the title already in place.
TermTextFolderMapping: The link between one folder of an instance and a category. A category leads to one folder per instance at most, and a folder with no category shows (unmapped).
TermTextGuardrails: The checks every apply passes before Routarr writes to an Arr: the global dry-run, the batch limit, the confirmation threshold, and whether the destination answers and has room. Some refuse and some ask you first, and the ones you can set are on the Guardrails tab of Settings.
TermTextInaccessible: The instance could not reach the folder at its last look, as when a NAS sleeps. The mapping stays, and an apply asks before writing there.
TermTextInactiveSource: A source in the active list that has no API key yet. It answers nothing until its key is saved.
TermTextInstance: A Radarr or Sonarr server Routarr connects to with its address and API key. Routarr reads its library and root folders, and writes to it only when a decision is applied or reverted.
TermTextInstanceEnabled: Only an enabled instance is synced and routed. A disabled one keeps its settings, and nothing is written to it.
TermTextLastSync: When Routarr last read the instance's titles and root folders. Never means it has not been read yet.
TermTextMaintenance: Removes the decisions, move log entries, tasks and security events older than the retention set in Settings, and clears data nothing uses any more.
TermTextMappedFolders: How many of the instance's root folders lead to a category. With none, its titles have nowhere to go.
TermTextMayConfirm: The guardrail questions this key may answer on its own: applying a whole simulation, more moves than the confirmation threshold, too little room, or a destination not answering. A question it may not answer is left to a person.
TermTextMetadataCache: How many days an answer stays fresh before the source is asked again. TMDB's answers are kept 180 days at most, as its terms require.
TermTextMetadataSource: A service Routarr asks for a title's genres, keywords, countries, ratings and languages. Radarr and Sonarr's own data is always read, and TMDB, OMDb, TheTVDB, AniList and Jikan (MyAnimeList) are added on Metadata sources, in the order you set.
TermTextMissingMetadata: Titles nothing is known about yet: no genres from their Arr and no answer from any source. Rules on genres, keywords or countries cannot match them.
TermTextMove: An apply changed the title's root folder in its Arr. Details shows the folder it left and the folder it went to.
TermTextMoveFiles: Whether the key may ask an apply or a revert to move files on disk. Without it, such a request is refused.
TermTextMoveLog: The record of every write to Radarr or Sonarr, one line per title moved or put back. A simulation writes nothing to an Arr and adds no line, and nothing is written while dry-run is on.
TermTextNoKey: Marks an operation that needs no key at all, such as /ping, which answers whether Routarr is up for an uptime monitor.
TermTextOperation: One method and path, such as GET /decisions, with what it does. Open it to see its parameters, its request body, its responses and an example.
TermTextOtherSite: A write sent from a page of another site, or a request sent to a host name this Routarr does not answer to, refused. Behind a reverse proxy, your own writes are refused this way when the proxy does not forward the public host.
TermTextOutcome: Success when the Arr took the write. Failure when it refused it, could not be reached or did not finish moving the files, with the reason in red in Details.
TermTextPerformedBy: Who asked for the write: the person the sign-in mode names, or the name of the application key that asked. It is empty when nobody asked or the mode names nobody.
TermTextPriority: The order rules are read in, lower numbers first. The first rule that matches wins, so a broad rule placed above a narrow one takes its titles.
TermTextProof: The password or the API key Routarr asks for again before a key is made or removed. A refused proof is a session that tried without it.
TermTextProposedCategory: The category the last simulation decided for a title. It reads not evaluated until a simulation has read the title, and a lock marks a category forced by an exception.
TermTextRefused: Routarr turned the request away: a wrong password, a key that opens nothing, a scope the key lacks, or a write from another site. Allowed rows are the sign-ins and changes that went through.
TermTextRepeated: Refusals anyone can send fast, such as a key that opens nothing or a write from another site, are written once a minute per address, with how many more came in that minute.
TermTextRequested: The move was sent with its files, and Radarr or Sonarr was still moving them when the apply stopped waiting. The next sync of the instance marks it Applied, or Failed if the Arr did not finish.
TermTextRevert: Moves an applied title back to the root folder it came from, and its files on disk too only if you tick that box. A reverted decision reads Skipped, marked reverted, and the move log records the revert.
TermTextRootFolder: A top folder Radarr or Sonarr stores titles under, as the Arr reports it. Each can be mapped to a category on Categories and folders, and Routarr moves a title by changing its root folder in the Arr.
TermTextRoutarrApiKey: The owner's key, which reaches everything, sent as X-Api-Key by scripts and monitoring. It is shown once when created or regenerated and cannot be read again.
TermTextRule: A set of conditions with a target category. Rules are read by priority, and the first that matches decides where the title goes.
TermTextRuleScope: What a rule applies to: movies, series or both, and the instances it is kept to. With no instance ticked, it applies to every instance.
TermTextRuleTest: A decision pinned as a test: a copy of one title and its metadata, with the category it must keep. Running the tests replays each copy against the rules as they stand, leaving exceptions out.
TermTextScheduler: Appears only when an unattended background pass stopped on an internal error. Syncing carries on, its detail names the cause, and the server log says more.
TermTextSchema: The named shape of what an operation takes or returns. A name shown beside a request body or a response is described in the Schemas card.
TermTextScope: What an application key may do, listed under Allows and shown as a badge on each operation of the API reference. Read is always held, and Operate, Write and Configure are granted one by one when the key is made.
TermTextScopeConfigure: Create, change or remove rules, categories, folder mappings, declared destinations and rule tests: what decides where every title goes.
TermTextScopeOperate: Sync, simulate, apply, revert, run the rule tests and take a backup. Only a key that operates may answer guardrails or move files.
TermTextScopeRead: Everything the screens show, except the settings, the keys and the backup archives. Every key holds it.
TermTextScopeWrite: Add or remove an exception, which forces a title's category.
TermTextSecurityEvent: The kind of thing that happened, such as Sign-in, API key, Application key or Settings. The Details column says what happened in a sentence.
TermTextSimulation: A pass that evaluates every rule against the whole library and records where each title belongs, writing nothing to Radarr or Sonarr. A Preview task is one an application asked for, which stores nothing either.
TermTextSourceApiKey: TMDB, OMDb and TheTVDB need a key of your own, pasted in the source's row or set in the environment variable the field names. It is stored encrypted, and a blank field keeps the stored key.
TermTextSourcePriority: The order of the active sources, highest first. The first source that has a value wins it, and the sources below fill in what it left empty.
TermTextSuperseded: A pending decision that a newer run replaced for the same title. It can no longer be applied, so the list hides it unless "Include decisions replaced by a newer run" is checked.
TermTextSync: Reading an instance's library and root folders into Routarr. It runs on each instance's own interval while Background sync is on, and on demand with Sync now or Sync all.
TermTextTask: One piece of background work, recorded from start to finish, with what it did in the Detail column. Its status is Running, Success, Failed, or Stopped when somebody stopped an apply or a revert.
TermTextTrigger: What set a task or a write off: Manual for a person in Routarr, Schedule for the background scheduler, Webhook for a notification from Radarr or Sonarr, Application for an application key, and Automatic for the work that follows a sync.
TermTextWebhook: An address Radarr or Sonarr calls when a title is added, imported, renamed or deleted. Routarr then decides where a new title goes right away instead of at the next sync.
TermTextWebhookToken: The secret that proves a webhook call comes from this instance, sent in the X-Routarr-Token header or inside the URL for an older Arr. Rotating it stops the Arr's webhook until the new value is pasted there.
WarnAutoApplyHeld: Automatic application is holding back {count} moves, more than the batch limit of {limit} allows in one unattended run. Apply them from the Simulation screen, or raise the batch limit.
WarnRadarrBelowVersion: {name} runs Radarr {version}, older than {minimum}, the oldest release Routarr supports in full: a film it adds is routed at the next sync, not before it downloads.
WarnSonarrBelowVersion: {name} runs Sonarr {version}, older than {minimum}, the oldest release Routarr supports in full: a series it adds is routed at the next sync, not before it downloads, and its original language is unknown.
WebhookTriggersRadarr: Tick On Movie Added, On Import, On Rename, On Movie Delete and On Movie File Delete.
WebhookTriggersSonarr: Tick On Series Add, On Import, On Rename, On Series Delete and On Episode File Delete.
WebhookUrlWithToken: Webhook URL for an older Arr
WebhookUrlWithTokenHelp: Radarr before 5.16 and Sonarr before 4.0.11 send no header: paste this address instead, the token in it.
RefreshTitleMetadataHint: Reads this title again from every source, and searches AniList and MyAnimeList for it anew.
TitleRefreshedByNone: No source answered. The next pass asks them again.
SourceRefreshHelp: Routarr reads a source's answers again once they are older than the cache lifetime. After a source corrects its data, read its answers again now.
SourceRefreshNone: No source to read again: Radarr and Sonarr's metadata comes with each sync.
